title: Scaling & Encoding Features
interviewAnswer: Scaling matters for distance- and gradient-based models; categorical encoding choices affect leakage, dimensionality and generalization. Tree models often need less scaling but still require correct category handling.
keyPoints: One-hot is robust for low-cardinality nominal categories.
why: Scaling & Encoding Features is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: Scaling matters for distance- and gradient-based models; categorical encoding choices affect leakage, dimensionality and generalization. Tree models often need less scaling but still require correct category handling. One-hot is robust for low-cardinality nominal categories. Target encoding requires leakage-safe folds/smoothing. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Fit the scaler/target encoder on training folds only, then transform validation/test.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Scaling & Encoding Features have?
How would you validate Scaling & Encoding Features on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
